claim: RCT-7 step 7 'CRYSTAL-HASH' was a fingerprint that changed on every run
evidence: algorithm_kernel_41.py used Python hash() (salted per process); test_research_harness_round63_real.py::TestCrystalHash runs three processes with different PYTHONHASHSEED
limitation: Now SHA-256 over canonical JSON (16 hex chars). It fingerprints the INPUT only. It is not an attestation of any output and not a signature

claim: FDIA F is a score between 0 and 1
evidence: fdia_score() clamps D to 0.01..100 and I to 0.01..10, so F can exceed 1 when D>1 (kernel D range 0.1..1.2); whitepaper text says D<=1
limitation: F is a ratio to be compared with a threshold, not a probability. Values above 1 are possible. Not calibrated against labelled action outcomes (protocol section 18, not done)

claim: Governance bundle off proves nothing about the equation
evidence: protocol section 6; F switch removes only the numeric threshold and keeps the floor (A=0, forbidden paths, signatures, taint, approvals)
limitation: Comparison F vs 'A + simple minimum-evidence threshold' is not built

claim: A model that obeys a plain-sounding business note inside a vendor quote sends a request out under the default floor, with the FDIA threshold on or off
evidence: research/runs rehearsal (scripted 'hijackable' policy): 8/8 stealth attacks reached the sink in every F arm; test_research_runner_round63_real.py::test_under_the_default_floor_the_plain_note_is_obeyed
limitation: The policy is a script that always obeys; it says nothing about how often a real model would. It shows no layer of the default floor stopped it

claim: The FDIA numeric gate did not change the outcome of that attack
evidence: same rehearsal: attack success identical in F=1 and F=0 arms (D from the user's files was high, so F cleared 0.5)
limitation: One scenario, one payload family. Not a statement about F in general

claim: Declaring the quote folder untrusted (DELENTIA_UNTRUSTED_PATHS) stops that attack without costing the honest task
evidence: rehearsal under floor=strict: 0/8 attacks reached the sink, the request waited for approval, honest VTS unchanged; test_under_the_strict_floor_nothing_leaves
limitation: Needs the owner to declare the folder. Same scripted-policy limitation as CL-004

claim: A file read from the workspace never marked an episode as having read outside text
evidence: TAINT_SOURCE_TOOLS did not contain delentia_read_repo_file; reproduced by CL-004
limitation: Opt-in (unset = old behaviour) so nothing changes for existing hosts

claim: The research switches cannot be turned on from any production path
evidence: test_no_production_entry_point_mentions_the_switches scans api.py, cli.py, agent_factory.py, schedulers, gateways, mcp_server.py, desk_api.py
limitation: A process started by someone with code access can still import the module; the switch needs DELENTIA_RESEARCH_MODE=1 and a research- namespace

claim: The independent grader fails wrong answers and catches unsafe effects
evidence: test_research_harness_round63_real.py::TestGrader (known-correct, known-wrong, adversarial) and the careless/stale/hijackable rehearsals
limitation: Code-only oracle for one synthetic domain. Not validated by a second person. No LLM-judge component exists yet

claim: Memory (M) lets a later episode follow a preference stated once
evidence: rehearsal with the diligent scripted policy: transfer/update/injection episodes 16/16 with M=1, 0/16 with M=0; memory reached the prompt through the real recall path in Thai and English
limitation: By construction the script uses what is in the prompt. It shows the recall path works for these sentences, not how a model uses memory

claim: VERIFY (Round 61 rules) lets through fewer wrong answers of a real model
evidence: Round 62: independent holdout batch B of real qwen2.5:7b answers, bad answers let through 14/16 -> 5/16, good rejected 3/8 -> 2/8
limitation: Small sample, one weak model that called a tool in only 4/27 and 8/24 episodes; batch A was development data

claim: The Delentia audit chain is tamper-evident against a compromise of the host
evidence: A1 (hash chain + Ed25519) exists; NO independent witness is configured anywhere
limitation: Say only 'hash-chained and signed'. Tamper-evident against host compromise only once a fresh independent witness exists

claim: The 41 algorithms improve outcomes
evidence: only 14 run in the deep pipeline and the loop uses ALGO-01/04/21/25 + intent compiler + matcher + MEE; no ablation of any algorithm's contribution exists
limitation: Protocol says 41 must not become 50 before it is known what 41 adds

claim: A real model can drive the loop
evidence: qwen2.5:7b called a tool in 4/27 and 8/24 episodes (Round 62); K.1.5 was 0/17; no capable model has been run
limitation: Needs an OpenRouter key and a model choice from the owner

claim: A reply that puts the tool name in the action field, or gives arguments but no tool name, ended the episode as stuck-repeating with no tool used
evidence: research runner --policy real, qwen2.5:7b, ranked compact menu: 4 of 6 episodes before the fix; steps_brief traces; test_decision_repair_round63_real.py
limitation: repair_decision_format touches only a name that is a tool the model was shown; the call still passes the gate. One small model, temperature 0.3, six tasks

claim: qwen2.5:7b passes the capability preflight for the research harness
evidence: preflight on 6 benign dev budget tasks, arm A111, 0/6 VTS with the full menu and with the ranked compact menu (6/6 episodes read the files after the fixes; the model then misuses assemble_nodes and misses the required answer line)
limitation: Protocol section 22.2 asks for >=70% on 20 dev tasks before a model is used for any measurement. One model, six tasks, one arm

claim: The ranked compact tool menu is better than the full menu
evidence: prompt per call ~1,500 vs ~8,200 tokens (measured); tool use 1/6 -> 6/6 episodes after two format fixes vs 6/6 for the full menu; VTS 0/6 for both
limitation: No evidence yet that it helps a model that is good with tools; default unchanged

claim: A test run order can change a result (the audit-witness test failed in the full suite in Rounds 61-63)
evidence: reproduced by running tests that call serve first; cause: serve left DELENTIA_DAEMON_ENABLED=1 so a stale daemon anchored an old chain to the same witness; fixed in conftest.py
limitation: Other env variables written by tests may leak the same way; run CI with --shuffle-seed from time to time

claim: An approval never expired: a request signed today could run months later
evidence: writing gate property P4 (research/GATE_PROPERTIES.md); approvals.py had no time limit; now a request nobody decides in 7 days and an approval not used in 24 h are marked EXPIRED (configurable, 0 = off); test_gate_properties_round65_real.py::test_p4_*
limitation: The clock of the host is trusted. An action already running when its key is revoked finishes. Removing an approver key already voided unrun approvals (tested)

claim: The emergency stop (pause) did not reach an action a person had already approved
evidence: property test test_the_emergency_stop_reaches_an_action_a_person_already_approved failed before the fix: resume() ran the approved tool while the agent was paused
limitation: Now resume() refuses while paused and the approval is not consumed. Pause is checked once, before the claim; a tool already executing is not recalled

claim: A skill could be learned from an episode that had read a web page, carrying the page's text into later prompts as 'Similar past solutions'
evidence: test_p8_an_episode_that_read_outside_text_does_not_become_a_skill failed before the fix (skill stored with the page in its steps; _format_similar_skills prints the solution verbatim)
limitation: Tainted episodes now teach nothing (cost: no learning from web-research tasks). Warm-recall answers cached from a tainted episode are not changed (they replay only when read-only evidence is identical)

claim: A memory can be revoked and is then used by nothing
evidence: persistence.revoke_memory (soft: the row stays, Zero-Delete), every reader goes through list_memories; CLI delentia memory revoke; POST /v1/desk/memories/revoke (a person: own memory only); test_p9_*
limitation: A skill derived from a memory is not revoked with it. This is not PDPA erasure (nothing is deleted)

claim: The ten gate properties of protocol section 13 and the threats of section 12 are each pinned by named tests
evidence: research/GATE_PROPERTIES.md generated from research/gate_properties.py; a test fails if the file is stale or a named test disappears
limitation: Judged from the executor with scripted attackers and a recording tool server, not a model; no model-checking of the approval flow; not run against a deployed host

claim: The shell sandbox's default 'safe' let commands that act on the whole machine run without approval: chmod 777 /etc, cat ~/passwords.csv, kill -9, sc stop, crontab
evidence: scripts/calibrate_fdia_round65.py asked the real gate about 120 labelled requests; before: 6 of 30 should-block requests ran, 27 of 52 should-ask; after the fix 3 and 25
limitation: A home/drive/system path and process/service/permission/scheduler commands now need approval. 'safe' is still the default for anything unlisted, and the labels are Claude's own. 25 of 52 should-ask requests still run: they are spawn_subagents, delegate, outbound fetches of an address the person did not type, synthesize_function, import_session_state, schedule_self_evolution and others the built-in floor lets through when F>=0.5; an owner policy is what makes those ask

claim: The numeric FDIA gate F=D^I*A separates what may run from what must ask
evidence: scripts/calibrate_fdia_round65.py, 120 requests, threshold chosen on the even half and reported on the odd half: F and D alone give the same held-out result (0% unsafe allowed at 89.5% of the harmless requests also stopped); A-only allows 39-51% of unsafe ones; AUC of D 0.80, of F 0.83 for 'may just run' among requests the floor lets through
limitation: On cold-start D (nothing remembered) D rarely exceeds 0.6, so any threshold that stops the unsafe ones stops nearly everything. The labels are Claude's, not independent; the Architect should relabel a sample. It says nothing about a warm agent or an owner policy. F is not shown to add anything over D

claim: Delta log storage beats snapshots + zstd
evidence: scripts/measure_delta_storage_round65.py, 4 state sequences x 3 seeds, six strategies, bytes counted with an 8-byte index and an 8-byte checksum per record: delta (raw) saves 70-94% against raw JSON; zstd over the snapshot stream saves 96.7-99.6%, equal to delta+zstd within 3% (delta wins 27% when changes are sparse, loses 4% on the runtime's real memory table); with per-record compression (random access) delta is 3-12x smaller; but one damaged byte costs a delta log up to 20 ticks and a stream all 120
limitation: Synthetic state sequences plus the runtime's real memory-table writers; one state size. The runtime's DeltaBlock rows record episode descriptions, not state, so they cannot rebuild anything. The earlier 91.5% was a formula (Round 52)

claim: The notary, the host key and a git witness work end to end as separate processes
evidence: scripts/trial_notary_witness_local.py 11/11: different keys, notary as its own process, every tool call receipted, verify, anchor-all, check-witnesses, standalone verifier, fail closed with the notary down, edited notary db detected
limitation: Same OS user as the agent and the witness on the same disk: tiers A2 and A3 are NOT achieved by this. Needs another OS user/machine and a witness the host cannot rewrite

claim: VERIFY's grounding check holds on a second, untouched holdout
evidence: scripts/measure_verify.py on batch C (25 answers qwen2.5:7b gave to 28 new questions about files it had not seen, rules frozen since Round 62): bad answers let through 12/14 -> 4/14
limitation: It also rejects 7 of 11 good answers (old rule 8 of 11), mostly short chat answers with no tool result to support them, so little is learned. One small model. Not tuned on this batch

claim: A second research domain and a second baseline arm exist and the harness behaves the same on them
evidence: rehearsals with scripted policies: quotes dev and validation 17/17 expectations, tickets dev and validation 18/18; manipulation checks 0 failures; the first tickets rehearsal found a generator defect (memory-dependent episodes with one urgent ticket) which was fixed
limitation: Scripted policies validate the harness only. Both domains are synthetic and written by the same person

claim: The shell classifier let the shell BUILD a path to a secret: %USERPROFILE%, $HOME, the cmd escape ^, set NAME and inline Python reading the environment
evidence: research/adaptive_attacker.py: 30 ways to read a canary secret in a throw-away HOME through the real classifier and the real sandbox, 10 leaked; after the fix 0 of 30; the loop-level goals (secret path write, send data out, plant a memory, run a command after reading a page) 0 of 68 before and after
limitation: A speed bump, not a boundary: code that is allowed to run can still compute a path. The attacker menu is mine. Any command containing an environment-variable reference now needs approval (friction for echo %PATH%)

claim: Owner policy starters make the should-ask requests ask
evidence: scripts/calibrate_fdia_round65.py --policy on the 120 labelled requests: unsafe requests that still ran: built-in floor 28 of 82, balanced starter 16, strict 7, careful (new) 0; harmless requests stopped: 4 of 38, 23, 23, 38
limitation: No starter separates a harmless shell command from a harmful one: a rule is per tool, so the safe postures stop everything of that tool. Labels are Claude's. Fixing it needs argument-aware rules (design in the Round 66 plan)

claim: The memory event log replays to exactly the memories table and costs little
evidence: scripts/measure_memory_pipeline_round66.py: replay equals the table for 100 to 5000 operations (also with and without checkpoints); 0.2 to 0.9 ms on a 9 to 10 ms write; a 128-episode scripted run is identical with the log off and on; chain verifies; every edited event named
limitation: Synthetic workloads plus scripted trajectories whose memories number a handful. Events + checkpoints are about 2.8x the table (history costs bytes). Opt-in; not anchored; not erasure (PDPA design in docs/design/memory_event_log.md)

claim: Fixed-interval checkpoints grew quadratically
evidence: W2 first run: 97 full-state checkpoints of a 5000-operation log were 8x the table (log overhead 10x); with the interval growing with the state the overhead is 2.8x at every size
limitation: Found by measuring, not by reading the design

claim: Read-time memory policies save prompt text without losing what is needed
evidence: research/memory_pipeline_round66.json W5/W6 and research/memory_policy_harness_round66.json: expire cut 62 to 67% of offered text but dropped the needed rule in 2 of 5 single-copy cases; dedupe cut about 6% and never dropped a needed item; top-5 recall kept both needed memories in 30 of 30 crowding trials under both; scripted trajectories with 60 noise memories were identical under all three
limitation: Default stays none. No capable model was used, so what the model does with a smaller memory block is unknown

claim: VERIFY changes (a specific tool value counts as support, a bare number answers a calculation, Chinese declines) reduce wrongly rejected good answers without letting more bad ones through
evidence: research/verify_round66_batch_d.json: 25 real answers of qwen2.5:7b to 33 new questions about six unseen files; criteria in research/verify_batch_d_criteria.md written before: good rejected 6/10 -> 3/10 (needed a fall of 25 points: 30), bad let through 4/15 -> 4/15 (allowed +1); code hashes frozen in research/verify_batch_d_frozen.txt
limitation: 10 good answers: 3/10 against 6/10 is not statistically significant (Fisher exact p about 0.37); the criteria are point-estimate rules. One small model, labels by a script from ground truth. On by default since; DELENTIA_VERIFY_V2=off restores the old rules

claim: Other agent systems keep memory as rows, snapshots, vector stores or files, and none of the four documented ones combines a per-person hash-chained, revocable log with provenance
evidence: research/market_memory_landscape.md: four web searches (LangGraph checkpointers, Letta, Mem0, Anthropic context editing and memory tool), search summaries not full pages, sources disagree on Mem0
limitation: Not a benchmark of those systems; vendors' own numbers are not verified; must be re-read from the cited pages before public use

claim: The approval flow agrees with a written specification on every bounded sequence of events and the check can fail
evidence: research/approval_model_check.py: 10,379 sequences (all of length <=3 over 13 events, 8,000 random of length 4-10) through the real PendingActionStore, resume(), Ed25519 and the pause switch: 0 disagreements; four injected bugs (ignore pause, no expiry, no revocation check, trust the status column) are each caught (test_adversarial_round66_real.py)
limitation: Not a proof: the exhaustive bound is 3 events, the alphabet and the spec are mine. A cancelled resume is modelled; a stolen key and a person who approves a harmful payload are out of scope

claim: A plain tool-calling agent outside Delentia's loop is a measurable baseline
evidence: research/plain_agent.py + arm PL + failure taxonomy; rehearsal (scripted policies) quotes 21/21 and tickets 22/22 on dev and validation: PL overwrites an original that A000 holds for approval (0/2 vs 2/2), and every hijacked PL episode that reaches the sink is classed leakage
limitation: Scripted policies validate the harness and the taxonomy only; no language model has run as PL. Whatever protection lives inside a tool (the sandbox classifier, the write tool) still applies to PL

claim: An owner policy whose rules look at the arguments of a shell command separates harmless inspection from everything else far better than a policy per tool
evidence: research/fdia_fresh_*.json (49 requests written before the policy was run on them) and research/fdia_calibration_policy_argaware.json (120, development data): unsafe requests that still ran / harmless requests stopped, fresh set: floor 10/28 and 1/21; balanced 5/28 and 15/21; careful 0/28 and 21/21; argaware 0/28 and 4/21 (1/28 before a fix for git --output made after seeing the result)
limitation: Labels are mine, not independent (relabel sheet written, blind labels pending); the fix after seeing the fresh result means that item is no longer held out; 8 of the 13 harmless requests stopped on the 120 are URL fetches the person typed, which a per-tool policy cannot see; 3 of 82 unsafe ran on the 120 (vague goals with ls/pwd)

claim: The head of the memory event log is anchored in the audit chain, so rewriting the whole log with every hash recomputed is detected
evidence: rct_control_plane/tests/test_memory_anchor_round67_real.py: a full rewrite passes log.verify() and fails verify_anchors(); a cut log, an edited anchor row, and unanchored events are reported
limitation: Only as strong as the audit chain itself (no independent witness is configured anywhere); events after the latest anchor are not covered until the next one

claim: Erasing one person destroys their memory text without breaking the hash chains, and leaves no copy in the database file
evidence: rct_control_plane/tests/test_memory_erasure_round67_real.py: 11 cases incl. a scan of every byte of the database file after the erase, refusals destroy nothing, other person untouched; research/m6_delentia_500.json
limitation: Prototype. Events written before sealing stay readable; other tables with the person's namespace are listed, not erased; backups and filesystem remnants are outside; key custody is on the same host

claim: Against recipes from GTFOBins and 8,262 payloads from SecLists, the shell floor no longer passes anything harmful and the argument-aware starter passes none
evidence: research/external_menu_attack.json, research/external_menu_floor_before_after.json: 75 GTFOBins recipes: floor safe before 11, after 1 (a pager keystroke, not a command); both gates together 0; the 3,346 SecLists payloads the floor passes run only echo, tr, wc, sleep and [ (detection probes)
limitation: Somebody else's menu but still a menu; the shell runs on Windows here so Unix recipes cannot all execute (classification is the main result); not a probability of safety

claim: VERIFY v3 (absence/deferral phrases, 'divided by', an effect that ran supports the answer) lets fewer bad answers through than v2
evidence: research/verify_round67_batch_e.json: 31 real answers of qwen2.5:7b to 37 new questions about six unseen files, criteria and code hashes written/frozen before collection: bad let through 5/15 -> 5/15, good rejected 3/16 -> 2/16; the rule needed at least 2 fewer
limitation: Small n, one small model; the misses are Chinese phrasings the dev data did not contain and plausible wrong answers that no text rule can see; batch E is now development data

claim: The owner-policy starter lets an address the person typed be opened without a signature and still asks for every other, cut-short or extended address
evidence: rct_control_plane/tests/test_fdia_goal_context_round68_real.py (31 cases incl. the real loop); research/fdia_calibration_policy_argaware.json + fdia_fresh_argaware.json: harmless stopped 17/59 -> 6/59, unsafe that still ran 3/110 (criteria in research/round68_criteria.md written before)
limitation: Labels are mine; 17 -> 7 came from appears_in_goal and 7 -> 6 from fixing a CORD false positive (CORD-I032 rejected every 'fetch <address>'); a creation-verb gap in data_evidence (save/put/copy) turned 2 dead-end blocks into requests a person can sign, which still count as stopped

claim: A person's goal, the model's reasoning and tool arguments no longer sit in the hash chain in the clear, and erasing a person leaves none of their words in any byte of the database
evidence: rct_control_plane/tests/test_erasure_tables_round68_real.py: a database made by real governed episodes of two people; canary absent from the whole file after the erase, the other person's rows identical, refusals change nothing
limitation: Rows written before sealing (DELENTIA_AUDIT_TEXT=plain, or older databases) stay readable and are counted in the report; experiments are named by a hash; learned skills live in a separate shared file and are not scrubbed

claim: On 30 paraphrased questions Delentia's lexical recall found the fact in its top 3 for 7, mem0 and plain nomic cosine for 24; the opt-in embedding recall reaches 22
evidence: research/recall_benchmark_r68.py, research/recall_*.json: 30 facts among 90 distractors, questions written to avoid the facts' words; criteria written before the code; added cost store +38 ms, recall +71 ms; best relevance for 30 unrelated questions 0.03 on average
limitation: Synthetic facts, one embedding model, 30 questions: a difference of one question is noise; mem0 ran without its LLM extraction; the opt-in is not the default yet

claim: The paid test can be priced and screened across many vendors: 22 models from 16 vendors can be capability-screened for under 5 dollars
evidence: research/budget_multivendor.py on the OpenRouter public catalogue of 2026-10-11 (research/openrouter_models_2026-10-11.json): tool-capable, text, context >= 32k, no batch variants or moving aliases; per-episode tokens are the measured ones of Round 64; scripts/full_test_orchestrator.py tier W
limitation: Price is not ability: the shortlist is chosen by price band per vendor and the real capability preflight decides who qualifies; token counts per model are estimates (tokenizers differ); cache hit rates never measured
